🔔 Money is rotating from Bitcoin into XRP. What the ETF flows show 

⚠️ Something unusual is happening in the flow of institutional money through crypto exchange-traded funds. In a single recent week, United States spot Bitcoin ETFs shed roughly $1.44 billion, the largest weekly outflow of 2026, while spot XRP ETFs did the opposite, drawing fresh money and extending a streak that has now reached six consecutive weeks of inflows. Those XRP funds have drawn around $1.44 billion since launching in November 2025. Ethereum funds bled too, losing hundreds of millions, while XRP and Solana products absorbed a combined couple hundred million. 

🌐 On the surface, the story writes itself: institutions are rotating out of Bitcoin and Ethereum and into XRP, a changing of the guard in where the smart money wants exposure. The flows are real and the divergence is striking. But what the rotation actually means is more complicated than the headline, and understanding the nuance is the difference between reading a genuine signal and overreading a small one. 

⚠️ This piece works through what the ETF flow data actually shows, why XRP is attracting money while Bitcoin bleeds, the crucial caveat about the relative size of these flows, what the rotation does and does not tell us about XRP’s prospects, why the inflows have not lifted XRP’s price, and how to read this kind of flow data without drawing more from it than it supports.

➡️From Vintage to MNTGE: Digital Fashion Brand to Release NFT Patches Linked to IRL Rewards

Digital fashion brand MNTGE is gearing up to release its Patchwork collection, comprised of a series of non-fungible token (NFT) patches paired with a physical counterpart.

MNTGE Patchwork features 13 unique digital patches designed by 11 artists including Jen Stark, Bored Ape Yacht Club artist Seneca and Nyan Cat meme creator Christopher Torres. The entire 7,500-unit collection will open for sale on July 27 on NFT marketplace OpenSea. Each NFT will be priced at 0.07 ETH, or $130, and the artwork will be revealed upon mint.

Each NFT is linked to an identical physical patch. Embedded with a near-field communication (NFC) chip, owners can scan the real-world patch to claim the digital token in their crypto wallet. By holding the patch on the blockchain and IRL, users can trace ownership as well as attend token-gated events and exclusive MNTGE experiences.

Additionally, the patches aren’t just one-off collectibles. In the physical world, they can be sewn onto MNTGE’s “base garments,” including t-shirts, jackets and denim. In the digital realm, the patches can be “owned” by the base garment itself. By implementing an ERC-6551 token standard, the digital wearable becomes a token-bound account that can custody the patches – creating an added layer of digital ownership.

Nick Adler, co-founder of MNTGE, told CoinDesk that the company was rooted in the goal of selling vintage fashion and utilizing the blockchain to revitalize its origins.

“People are out there wearing [vintage] and collecting it…young kids want to be authentic,” said Adler. “They don't want a Hot Topic shirt, they want the original shirt, right? So we just saw this natural, really honest use case for the blockchain, and we just felt like the two could really go hand in hand.”

As we predicted, the hype around TON DNS has begun. The hype began with Four-Digit domains (hereinafter referred to as 4N domains). People are "burning" their 100 TON on the TON DNS smart contract and transferring this value to NFTs (similar to Banksy's work). 

On February 13, the last domain from the Club 100 (0074.ton), was minted, on February 17, the thousandth domain (5755.ton), and on February 28, the last domain from the 1k Club (0863.ton).

The race is on, and people have already minted many beautiful numbers from various masks and special collections, although only 26% of the total supply has been minted.

On average, 117 4N domains are minted per day. At the current rate, 50% of the supply will be minted by March 22, 2026, 75% by April 12, 2026, and 100% by May 4, 2026. 

Why 4N domains if there are already Telegram usernames?

1. Numbers are the international language of communication. They are simple and understandable for everyone around the world, unlike various alphabets (be it Latin, Cyrillic, Arabic, hieroglyphs, etc.).

2. There are 10^4 = 10,000 number combinations in 4N domains, compared to 26^4 = 456,976 combinations in alphabetical ones.

3. The price for the 4L username is fixed at $8,000. The price for the 4N domain on mint is approximately $130, which is 61.54 times cheaper!

4. Only domains can consist of numbers, while usernames must contain at least one letter. Therefore, 4N domains are beyond competition in the TON ecosystem.

5. The ability to associate attractive domain digits with a gift number. An example is here. There are dozens of different collections of gifts with identical numbers, but only one 4N domain can be associated with them!

6. The TON ecosystem will have thousands of AI agents, and they will need a short digital domain for convenience.

7. TON Browser and TON Messenger are being developed, with user login via TON DNS.

8. Repeating the success of ENS, this time in the form of a utility — a shell in Telegram (because TON DNS renewal costs pennies, compared to $160 per year for a 4-digit ENS).

🔊 Iranian and Pakistani ministers discuss expanding scientific, research cooperation

📌 Tehran, IRNA—Minister of Science, Research and Technology Hossein Simaei Sarraf, while welcoming the expansion of scientific cooperation between Iran and Pakistan, has suggested the necessary preparations to enroll brilliant Pakistani students in the University of Sistan and Baluchestan for higher education.

Simaei Sarraf made the announcement as he met with Wajiha Qamar, Pakistan's Minister of State for Federal Education and Professional Training, on the sidelines of the Türkiye Educational Technologies Summit (TETZ) in Istanbul, organized by the Turkish Education Ministry, on Saturday.
​
During the meeting, the two ministers emphasized that the historical, religious and cultural commonalities between the two neighbors give them an opportunity to expand the existing relations to others fields, including education and research.
​
Stating that the hearts of the people of the two countries are close to each other, Simaei Sarraf expressed disappointment over the level of scientific, academic, technological and innovation cooperation between Iran and Pakistan, saying these are necessary to benefit both countries.
​
He also commended the Pakistan government and people for their support to the Iranian nation during the recent war imposed by the United States and the Israeli regime.
​
For her part, the Pakistani minister, while welcoming the expansion of scientific cooperation, proposed the establishment of a joint scientific working group between Iran and Pakistan.
​
Stating that Iran's achievements in different arenas are inspiration for many countries, Wajiha Qamar said the people of Pakistan were also eager to take the Iranian path as a model.
​
Pakistan can benefit from Iran's valuable experiences in the fields of skills training, agriculture, construction, and production, and the deep linguistic, religious, and civilizational ties between the two countries provided a suitable platform for expanding this cooperation, she added.

Today, I’m joined by Ben Zhou — billionaire, founder and CEO of Bybit, and one of the people building the infrastructure for a new era. Under his leadership, the company has grown into a global powerhouse serving 81 million users across 243 countries, with more than $19 billion in daily trading volume. Today, Bybit is the world’s second-largest cryptocurrency exchange.

In this episode, we break down how blockchain technology is becoming the backbone of the new economy and why stablecoins are already processing more transaction volume than Visa and Mastercard. We also discuss what lies ahead for traditional banks — whether they can adapt or whether they’ll fade away like pagers in the age of smartphones.
